thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-CH: P12345 -> Severity: SEV2. Trigger: AZ5 serving-degrade - high 5xx rate and token generation latency spike. Link: https://pd.local/alerts/P12345 :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: Alert routed to marta (oncall-sre). Auto-escalation in 8m.
marta (oncall-sre): Acked oncall. I'm looking. Initial note: saw a big jump in 5xx from model shards in az5, plus connection resets from nic.
eli (net-eng): I'm pulling NIC metrics for az5 fabric. Any immediate customer impact numbers?
alice (support): Some customers reported degraded chat responses and timeouts, support tickets #4321 #4322 referencing 504s. Not yet widespread but multiple tenants in eu-west region.
marta (oncall-sre): Confirmed. Top-10 customers: 3 with >50% failed requests. Estimated RPS affected: ~1200 (regional peak).
pagerduty-bot: PD: escalation step 1 -> rajan (senior-oncall) notified.
rajan (senior-oncall): On call. Marta, status and plan?
marta (oncall-sre): Hypothesis: transient NIC packet loss + autoscaler lag causing overload and KV prefix cache thrashing. Plan: 1) temporarily divert new traffic away from az5 to az3/az2 routing pool; 2) scale up dedicated capacity in az5 (if safe) and trigger graceful evacuate of model shards; 3) enable fallback variant (lower mem) for heavy models to reduce eviction. Seeking quick ack to divert.
sam (platform-op): Divert ok if we do staged shift (10% -> 30% -> 100) to avoid cascading load. I'll prepare the routing change.
eli (net-eng): NIC shows sporadic rx errors and retransmit spike starting 4m ago in az5-rt-2. Networking team advising we should not fully fail az5 yet but reduce inbound.
statusbot: Suggested status page update draft: "We are investigating increased errors and latencies affecting inference (eu-west AZ5). We may temporarily divert traffic to nearby zones; some customers may see degraded performance." Want to post?
alice (support): Post now as "investigating" with mention of potential diversion. Good to let customers know.
marta (oncall-sre): Execute diversion config. Sam, once you start, will watch for error rates. Command to shift route pools:
```
# staggered reroute via routerctl
routerctl set-weight az5 80
routerctl set-weight az3 110
sleep 30
routerctl set-weight az5 60
routerctl set-weight az3 140
sleep 30
routerctl set-weight az5 30
routerctl set-weight az3 170
```
Start now.
sam (platform-op): Starting step 1 -> setting az5->80%. Pushing.
incident-bot: Automation note: prefix-cache rehydrate queued for az3 on new traffic.
marta (oncall-sre): Watching dashboards. 5xx rate dropping from 18% -> 9% on diverted traffic. Latency median still up ~240ms.
rajan (senior-oncall): Good. Next: if we see further drop, continue to 30% weight. Also trigger canary fallback variant on heavy models in az5 to free memory:
```
deployctl rollout model-variant vm-compact --zone az5 --percentage 20
```
marta (oncall-sre): Rolling 20% now.
eli (net-eng): NIC errors reduced slightly after partial divert. But we still see retransmits. NOC recommends planning for shard evacuation if packet loss persists.
sam (platform-op): Autoscaler: manual scale +2 gpus in az5 attempted; resource quota limited. Requesting approval to borrow burst capacity from reserved pool.
rajan (senior-oncall): Approve borrow for 30 minutes if it helps stabilize. Authorize now.
sam (platform-op): Borrow issued, scaling +2 nodes. Starting graceful shard migration for hot models off az5.
alice (support): I'll update status page: "We are diverting traffic and performing mitigation; some customers in eu-west may see degraded results. Engineers are actively working on a fix." Posting now.
statusbot: Status page updated: incident 2026-03-15-AZ5-001 created.
pagerduty-bot: PD note: marta acknowledged; incident severity remains SEV2. Escalation timer paused.
marta (oncall-sre): Evac migration started. Shrinking workloads on az5, verifying KV cache persistence.
incident-bot: Automated healthcheck detected model shard rehome complete for 3 hot shards.
marta (oncall-sre): After shard migration, 5xx dropped to 3% in diverted flow, total region 6%. Good signal.
eli (net-eng): NIC errors still show small blips; we should keep diversion to 30% for now and monitor for 20 more mins before full reintroduce.
rajan (senior-oncall): Agree. Keep diversion and continue checking. Begin preparing postmortem notes: suspected root cause = transient NIC degradation exacerbated by autoscaler lag and cache thrash.
sam (platform-op): I'll schedule automated reintroduce script to slowly rebalance:
```
# reintroduce plan
routerctl bump az5 +10 every 2m until back at normal weight
monitoring alert: if 5xx > 5% for 3m -> stop and roll back
```
marta (oncall-sre): Do not reintroduce until NOC gives clean bill.
eli (net-eng): NOC says fabric firmware shows partial packet drop; they're deploying a conservative fix but it will take 12-20m.
alice (support): Customers notified of ongoing mitigation. No escalation to executive yet; only affected tenants notified.
pagerduty-bot: PD: incident notes appended.
marta (oncall-sre): I'll remain on this thread until handoff. Timeline: mitigation in progress, expect stable in 30-45m. If anything spikes, page again.
rajan (senior-oncall): Pairing handoff to rajan in 45m for postmortem and follow-ups.
incident-bot: Auto-log created: incident/1789999990/az5-evac.
statusbot: Will update status page when metrics stabilize.
alice (support): Thanks everyone. I'll keep support looped for any customer callbacks.
rajan (senior-oncall): Thanks team. Keep concise updates only.
marta (oncall-sre): Update: +2 nodes are healthy, migration completed for priority shards, error rates stable. Leaving thread but will check back in 20m.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: marta -> acknowledged -> status: monitoring.
statusbot: Incident note: mitigation successful so far; investigating root cause. Will transition to follow-up channel once stable. :white_check_mark:
